title: Procurement Financial Acceptance & Invoice Audit Playbook
author: Asha Patel
body:
Overview
--------
This playbook defines the financial acceptance, invoice audit, and handoff procedures that connect procurement execution to billing and revenue recognition at Redwood Inference. It formalizes: acceptance criteria for goods/services, automated and manual invoice validation rules, the 3-way match policy, exception workflows, SLA timelines, ownership, and the downstream handoff to billing and revenue recognition teams.

Scope
-----
Applies to: all vendor purchases that are invoiced to Redwood (cloud services, dedicated hardware, software licenses, professional services, and one-time procurement). Does not replace contract-level special procedures for high-value/strategic agreements (> $5M ARR equivalent) which follow a separate commercial playbook — see Related Pages.

Definitions
-----------
- Financial Acceptance: Formal confirmation (PO or equivalent) that the organization accepts a supplier deliverable from an accounting/budget perspective, enabling invoice processing.
- 3-way Match: Matching of PO, receipt/acceptance evidence, and supplier invoice to verify payment validity.
- GRN (Goods Received Note): Record created by requestor or receiving team confirming receipt of physical goods or completion of services.
- Commit Trigger: Event that notifies RevRec team to consider revenue-affecting obligations (applies primarily to customer contracts; included here for completeness where procurement impacts billing).

High-level Process Overview
---------------------------
1. Purchase Order (PO) created and approved via Procurement system.
2. Supplier delivers goods/services. Requestor or Receiving creates a GRN or completion ticket and tags PO number.
3. Supplier submits invoice to invoices@redwood-accounts.example (or portal).
4. Invoice routed to AP for automated validations and 3-way match.
5. Matches pass to finance acceptance step; mismatches generate exceptions routed to owners.
6. Accepted invoices are coded, approved, and queued to pay cycles.
7. For expense types impacting revenue recognition (e.g., pass-through customer billings, marketplace fees, capacity commitments), billing/RevRec receives a notification and the ledger mapping is updated.

Acceptance Criteria (Financial)
------------------------------
Invoices and supporting evidence must satisfy all of the following before financial acceptance: 
- Valid PO number that is active and not closed.
- Supplier identity matches contract record (vendor ID).
- Invoice amount and currency align with PO or approved change order.
- Receipt evidence (GRN, completed ticket, or sign-off email) dated on or before invoice date.
- For recurring services, there must be a contract/statement of work (SOW) and an approved renewal/endorsement if beyond original term.

Invoice Submission and Routing
------------------------------
- Preferred submission: supplier portal or invoices@redwood-accounts.example with structured PDF or machine-readable invoice (UBL/Peppol or JSON).
- Invoices must include: supplier legal name, vendor ID, PO number, invoice date, invoice number, line-level descriptions, tax amounts, and remittance details.
- Files are auto-ingested into AP system (Coupa/NetSuite connector or bespoke ingestion pipeline).
- Ingestion validation checks: checksum, required fields, duplicate invoice detection (30 day window), allowed currency.

Automated Validation Rules (examples)
------------------------------------
1. Duplicate detection: identical supplier + invoice amount + invoice date. Flag threshold: 90% match = potential duplicate.
2. PO status: PO must be APPROVED and not fully invoiced beyond tolerance (5% overage allowed for freight/handling unless capped in PO).
3. Tax validation: VAT/GST presence validated for jurisdiction; missing tax IDs routed for manual review.
4. Currency mismatch policy: If invoice currency != PO currency and FX impact > $500, route to Finance for pre-approval.

3-way Match Policy
------------------
- Strict 3-way match required for goods and capital equipment (PO + GRN + invoice).
- Tolerant match allowed for services and professional services with SOW: invoice may match PO lines with supporting completion ticket; tolerance 10% per line, 7 calendar days timing variance.
- For small purchases (<= $2,500), AP may perform 2-way match (PO + invoice) at AP discretion.
- Any match failing automated rules becomes an "Exception" and follows Exception Workflow below.

Exception Workflow
------------------
1. AP flags exception and creates an exception case in the procurement ticketing system (link to case).
2. Exception owner assigned based on type: 
   - Receipt missing: requestor (originating cost center).
   - PO mismatch: Procurement owner.
   - Price variance > tolerance: Finance owner + Procurement.
   - Duplicate suspicion: AP fraud desk.
3. SLA for remediation: 5 business days for receipt/matching evidence; 10 business days for price disputes.
4. If unresolved after SLA, escalation to Procurement Director and Legal for potential hold or payment stop.

SLA, Timelines and Payment Cycle Integration
-------------------------------------------
- Standard AP payment runs: 15th and last business day of month; expedited runs allowed for vendor risk (fraud or SLA exposure).
- Target throughput: 90% of valid invoices accepted (no manual intervention) within 48 hours of receipt.
- Exception reduction targets: reduce exceptions by 20% year-over-year via supplier outreach and PO discipline.

Revenue Recognition Handoff Rules
--------------------------------
While procurement is generally an expense flow, certain procurement items drive billing or RevRec implications (examples: capacity commitments, marketplace pass-through, and contracted third-party metering). For these items: 
- Tag invoice lines with RevRec impact flag in AP system (field: revrec_flag = TRUE).
- When revrec_flag is true, AP must attach: related customer contract ID (if pass-through), allocation mapping, and the recognized revenue schedule or trigger note.
- Notification: AP triggers an automated notification to revenue-recognition@redwood.example with invoice ID, PO, and supporting evidence.
- RevRec team has 3 business days to respond with ledger mapping; if no response, default codings apply but RevRec will retroactively adjust if required (documented adjustments required in change log).

Controls and Audit Steps
------------------------
- Monthly sampling: Finance performs a 30-invoice statistical sample per supplier tier (Tier A: > $1M/year, Tier B: $250k-$1M, Tier C: < $250k) to validate compliance with 3-way match and coding.
- Quarterly internal audit: review of exception backlogs, aging >30 days, and FX policy adherence.
- Retention: invoices and supporting evidence must be retained for 7 years per legal policy.

Roles & Responsibilities (RACI summary)
--------------------------------------
- Requestor: Create GRN, confirm delivery or service completion (Responsible).
- Procurement: Validate PO changes, vendor relationship and contract alignment (Accountable/Consulted).
- Accounts Payable (AP): Ingest, perform automated match, code invoice, route exceptions (Responsible).
- Finance (General Ledger & Costing): Review FX impacts, chart of accounts mappings, and revenue flags (Accountable).
- RevRec Team: Map invoice lines that affect revenue recognition and confirm ledger treatment (Consulted/Responsible for RevRec items).
- Legal: Support disputes, contract interpretation on pricing and change orders (Consulted).

Escalation Matrix
-----------------
1. Day 0–5: Case owner (AP/Procurement/Requestor) resolves.
2. Day 6–10: Procurement Manager / AP Manager notified.
3. Day 11–15: Procurement Director + Finance Manager escalate decision (pay/hold/cut check under protest).
4. > Day 15: Legal and VP Finance involved; potential suspension of vendor payments until legal resolution.

Templates and Examples
----------------------
- Required email subject for supplier invoice submission: "Invoice Submission | VendorID XXXX | PO #YYYYYY"
- Minimum JSON invoice schema accepted by ingestion pipeline (example):
{
  "vendor_id": "V-12345",
  "invoice_number": "INV-2026-9876",
  "invoice_date": "2027-01-10",
  "po_number": "PO-54321",
  "currency": "USD",
  "lines": [
    {"description": "NVIDIA A100 80GB instance hours", "quantity": "100", "unit_price": "10.00", "line_total": "1000.00", "revrec_flag": "false"}
  ],
  "total": "1000.00"
}

- Sample GRN entry template (text): "GRN | PO-54321 | Received 2026-12-15 | Quantity 20 | Received by: S. Lim | Notes: Rack-mount units inspected, serials logged."

Operational Improvements & Continuous Reduction of Exceptions
------------------------------------------------------------
- Quarterly supplier workshops to improve invoice format and PO discipline.
- Automation investments: increase structured invoice adoption to 75% of supplier spend within 12 months.
- Business partner reviews: procurement & finance to run monthly exception cadence to surface systemic issues to engineering (for APIs and invoice portals).

KPIs and Reporting
------------------
- GL coding accuracy: target 98% on first-pass.
- Invoice straight-through processing (STP): target 90% within 48 hours.
- Exception aging: <10% >30 days.
- RevRec impact notification SLA: 3 business days response rate 95%.
